clue.text: Supporters will get no cover like this

definitions.text: Supporters will get no cover like this

parts.words: Supporters will get no cover like this
parts.note: the supporters are a person's legs, and with no covering of tights or trousers they are left exposed

explanation.surface: A warning that fans or backers will be left unprotected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' suggests fans or backers, but here it means the legs that hold a person up.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without stockings or trousers leaves the lower limbs uncovered, which is the whole picture the clue paints.

clue.text: Sort of paint finish that's apt to crack?

definitions.meaning: a low-sheen paint finish between matt and gloss
the fragile casing of a hen's egg, which breaks easily

explanation.surface: A decorator worries about a paint finish that tends to craze.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a semi-matt paint sheen and the brittle outer casing laid by a hen, famously quick to break.

clue.text: In taking bet, show a view

indicators.note: the word for 'In' takes the bet inside it, as a container holding its contents

parts.note: in and at are interchangeable (at home = in)
spec, short for speculation, is a gamble or bet

explanation.surface: Someone at the bookmaker's places a bet and gets to see a view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is just a link here between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A house's outlook or prospect in a given direction is called its facing, a view.

clue.text: Lost vitality, being made to conserve energy

indicators.note: to conserve something is to keep it safely within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: made, as in carried out, can be did
E is the standard symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A tired person flags while being forced to save energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To have perished is to have lost all life and vitality; figuratively a thing that faded away.

clue.text: Perhaps sense number in churches is showing decline

indicators.note: perhaps tells us the word sense is only one possible arrangement of its letters
in places the number inside the pair of churches

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England, so two churches give CE twice

explanation.surface: Perhaps a feeling of how many attend church shows congregations dwindling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' turns SENSE into SENES; 'in' puts N inside CE CE to make CENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The scientific word for growing old describes a gradual deterioration with age.

clue.text: Civic dignitary for a month or less (there's no latitude)

parts.note: May is a month of the year

indicators.note: there's no tells us one letter is dropped from the word less

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for latitude on maps

explanation.surface: A town official serves a term of a month or under, with no room for manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's no' removes the L of latitude from LESS, leaving ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman holding the office of town mayor, or the mayor's wife, is a civic dignitary.

clue.text: Stars, say, getting up

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Stars, say, getting up (6)' supplies only EG reversed; no words give the MINI/INIM of GEMINI, so the clue is cut short or garbled and no scan or search gives the rest.

clue.text: Yield in course of peace deliberations

indicators.note: the answer is found running within the course of the following words

explanation.surface: A negotiator gives ground partway through peace talks.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up territory or a point is to yield it to another party.

clue.text: Saint turning out to be genius at university?

indicators.note: turning out signals the letters are rearranged to produce something new

explanation.surface: A clever student at college might become a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' anagrams GENIUS, AT and U; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustine of Hippo, the early Church Father, is venerated as a saint.

clue.text: Tree from Matabeleland

indicators.note: from tells us to take the letters out of the place name that follows

explanation.surface: A tree native to a region of southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The white poplar is also known by this name, so it is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Terrible need overwhelms a street in poor area of London

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the scrambled word surrounds the other pieces
terrible suggests the word need is badly mangled

explanation.surface: Dire poverty engulfs a road in a deprived district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' turns NEED into E...END, which 'overwhelms' A ST.
explanation.definitionFit: The eastern part of the British capital was historically its poorest working-class district.

clue.text: Ecstasy's the reason for showing a lot of feeling

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a motive is a reason for acting

explanation.surface: A drug is the cause of someone becoming very emotional.
explanation.definitionFit: Language or behaviour that stirs strong emotion is described this way.

clue.text: There's yet time for the race?

parts.note: yet and even both intensify a comparison (yet more, even more)

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they can still make it to the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A single contest in an athletics meeting is called an item on the programme, a race.

clue.text: Old scientist, a Liberal, joining Church Times after changes

parts.note: L abbreviates Liberal in British politics

indicators.note: after changes means the word Times is rearranged

explanation.surface: A Liberal starts working for the Church Times newspaper after some reshuffles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after changes' anagrams TIMES to EMIST. The Church Times is a British Anglican weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval practitioner trying to turn base metals into gold was a forerunner of the chemist.

clue.text: Extreme hatred show Bacon here, perhaps? That's about right

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the next piece
perhaps hints that the letters of Bacon here may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A gallery visitor hates the idea of a Francis Bacon exhibition being shown here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' anagrams BACON HERE to ABHO...RENCE, which goes 'about' R. Francis Bacon was a British painter of disturbing images.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing or detestation is intense hatred.

clue.text: Melodramatic articles Thailand and two US states

parts.note: the and a are the definite and indefinite articles
T is the international vehicle registration code for Thailand
RI is Rhode Island and CAL is California

explanation.surface: Overwrought newspaper pieces about Thailand and a couple of American states.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaggerated, stagey behaviour is like acting on stage.

clue.text: Something to bank on getting — a firm farewell?

definitions.text: Something to bank on getting — a firm farewell?

parts.words: Something to bank on getting — a firm farewell?
parts.note: a firm here is a company, and its farewell to a departing executive is a large lump sum to put in the bank

explanation.surface: A dependable sendoff with a solid grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like an adjective for a strong grip but means a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous payment given to a senior employee on leaving a company is a farewell gift of money.

clue.text: See primate take vermouth provided as pre-dinner drink

parts.note: an ape is a primate
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
provided and if both introduce a condition

explanation.surface: An ape drinks vermouth as a cocktail before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link; 'take' as R comes from the abbreviation on old prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetiser drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Unknown quantity a nightmare, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a person whose abilities are not yet known
a mare out at night would be a black steed

explanation.surface: Something unpredictable turns out to be a bad dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a little-known competitor who may surprise, and literally a black-coated steed, as a mare at night might be.

clue.text: Was sorry about fellows having frills round neck

indicators.note: about means around, so the regret surrounds the fellows

parts.note: rued means regretted, was sorry
FF is the plural abbreviation of fellow

explanation.surface: Someone regrets surrounding a group of men wearing frilly collars.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruff is a pleated Elizabethan collar, so a person wearing one has frills at the throat.

clue.text: Robin's contribution we hear taking precious time?

parts.note: twee means affectedly precious or cute

explanation.surface: Birdsong from a robin seems quaint and precious.
explanation.definitionFit: A short chirp of a small bird is what a robin contributes to the dawn chorus.

clue.text: Dutch navigator is relaxed about one four on board

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Dutch navigator is relaxed about one four on board (6)': no parse gives TAS + MAN with every word a job ('is relaxed', 'one four'); the text looks garbled and no scan or search confirms it.

clue.text: Arbiter about to face charge, kidnapping monarch

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: kidnapping means seizing and holding, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a fee is a charge
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A judge is about to face a criminal charge for abducting a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A match official who decides disputes is an arbiter.

clue.text: Support for potter

parts.note: a potter here is a snooker player who pots balls, and the cue is propped on a special stick

explanation.surface: Something to help a craftsman at the pottery wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potter' suggests a ceramicist; it is a snooker player.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker the stick with a crossed head used to prop up a cue is named for giving support.

clue.text: Composer's son is playing in Rhode Island

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of son is are being played around with

explanation.surface: A composer's son is performing in a New England state.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: To go up part of stair easy

clue.text: Woman graduate becomes queen of ancient nation

parts.note: she refers to a woman
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A female graduate becomes a queen in the ancient world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes queen of' is a link, nodding to the biblical Queen of Sheba.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical kingdom in southern Arabia, ruled by a famous queen, was an ancient nation.
